identity_notes: Unlike valine, L-leucine has a genuinely large, direct human oral-supplementation evidence base, concentrated in sarcopenia/muscle-protein-synthesis research. However, three major false-match clusters inflate the raw retrieval: (1) LRRK2 ('leucine-rich repeat kinase 2') Parkinson's disease drug trials, (2) LGI1 ('leucine-rich glioma inactivated 1') autoimmune encephalitis studies, and (3) microcystin-leucine-arginine cyanotoxin studies -- all rejected as off_topic false keyword matches. A further ~15 records concern N-acetyl-L-leucine/levacetylleucine, a chemically modified PHARMACEUTICAL form used in rare neurological diseases (Niemann-Pick C, ataxia-telangiectasia); these were rejected as different_substance since they are a distinct regulated drug entity, not the dietary L-leucine supplement. HMB (beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate), a leucine METABOLITE frequently co-studied or reviewed alongside leucine, was also rejected as different_substance throughout. Among genuine L-leucine (or leucine-dominant-combination) trials, the evidence for SARCOPENIA/muscle mass in older adults is the largest and most consistent body, but results are decidedly mixed at the level of individual RCTs -- several well-powered, well-designed trials found NO benefit of leucine alone on muscle mass, strength, or function (19321567, 34358827, 40926079, 41580240, 37375630), while others found positive effects, often specifically when leucine was combined with vitamin D and/or resistance exercise (26170041, 32230954, 40381110) rather than as a monotherapy. A 2025 meta-analysis (40805998, 566 leucine-arm participants) and an umbrella review (32483625) both lean positive but grade the evidence as low quality, and note leucine's benefit is 'restricted when used alone without concurrent additional therapy.' The great majority of kept records deliver leucine as part of a combination product (whey/EAA/vitamin D blends, BCAA mixtures, omega-3/probiotic foods) rather than isolated free L-leucine, and are flagged related_form_differs accordingly -- reviewers should weight the small number of clean leucine-alone RCTs (19321567, 32191600, 32230954, 33310174, 38088883, 39854288, 40926079, 41580240, 41786247) most heavily for a single-ingredient label claim. Two very old (pre-1980), abstract-less case reports document leucine-induced/leucine-sensitive reactive hypoglycemia and are routed to handoff safety.
